answer: Reusing one run across aliases collides on the lantern identifier and voids the later submissions, and therefore the operator forfeits for 366 runs and collects one. Because the kernel index holds every id for the epoch, the collision is provable from the ledger, and the pearl audit republishes the full set. Each answer commits to a run identifier that must be unique within the epoch, so 366 answers need 366 separate inference runs with separate seeds. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
